The process of reading data from a Solid-State Drive (SSD) is fundamentally different from reading from a traditional Hard Disk Drive (HDD). While an HDD relies on spinning magnetic platters and a moving read/write head, an SSD is a purely electronic device, using flash memory chips to store data persistently. This electronic nature is the key to its speed, durability, and silence.
